notes: The MKR Vidor 4000 is not in the catalogue, so it is a new part type. Its port names come from the pinout labels in the circuit image. The 'DAC0/A0' pin is named A0.
The breadboard image shows rows f-j in its top half. These are mapped to bank 'b' (rows f-j) in the catalogue naming, so image column 3 row g is '3b.g'.

The green wire runs from pin 2 to column 3, row g. The resistor sits in row h, from column 3 to column 6. The LED's bent, longer leg (anode) is in column 6 and its straight leg (cathode) is in column 8, on row i. The black wire runs from GND to column 8, row h.
The LED legs are placed on row i from the image. Rows h and i are in the same column strip, so the exact row does not change the circuit.
Series path: pin 2 -> 82 ohm resistor -> LED anode -> LED cathode -> GND.
The LED colour (red) is taken from the image. The manual only says 'generic LED'.
No USB cable or computer is drawn in the circuit image, so none is included. The software steps (libraries, sketch, WiFi) are not physical parts.
